ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Status indicators, accent dots, live signals, decorative fills — the sole chromatic note in an otherwise monochrome system

onyx.$description: Onyx — Dark hero background, deep badges, section dark-mode surfaces

graphite.$description: Graphite — Primary text, nav links, body copy, filled button text

stone.$description: Stone — Secondary text, heading subtitles, supporting copy

ash.$description: Ash — Muted helper text, inactive nav state, subtle UI metadata

silver-mist.$description: Silver Mist — Hairline dividers, grid lines, light borders, low-emphasis text

fog.$description: Fog — Light body backgrounds, subtle section washes, nav inactive background

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas, base background surface

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Card surfaces, elevated panels, tag borders, card borders

display-fade-gradient.$description: Display Fade Gradient — Gradient fill on massive display type — black fading to mid-gray to light silver across the word

horizon-gradient.$description: Horizon Gradient — Section transitions and hero vignette — horizontal black to silver fade

die-grotesk-b.$description: Primary workhorse grotesque used for body text, mid-scale headings, labels, captions, and links. Weight 500 across all sizes creates a uniform visual density — no weight contrast, hierarchy comes purely from size and color. Tighter letter-spacing at larger sizes (-0.03em at 60px) tightens the grotesque into near-condensed proportions.

abc-gravity-variable.$description: Monument-scale super-condensed display face. Used only for hero statements and section openers that fill the viewport. The extremely tight line-height (0.74) lets massive 288px letters stack with minimal vertical air — letters physically touch or nearly touch, creating a wall of type. Variable weight axis allows subtle weight shifts even at this scale.

ibm-plex-mono.$description: Technical voice for metadata, timestamps, nav labels, status text, and icon-adjacent micro-copy. Always uppercase, always small (12–14px). The monospaced rhythm signals 'system data' and contrasts against the grotesque's proportional flow — it reads as a developer/designer interface layer over the editorial body.
